title: What does a strict score do to progress?
hook: Six models, each a bit better per word than the last. Graded strictly, how do they look?

knows: a whole answer's probability is the product of its tokens' (long-answers-lose-the-product, greedy-word-trap)
doesNotKnow: that an all-or-nothing score on a multi-token answer turns a smooth per-token improvement into a curve that sits near zero and then shoots up, so a "sudden ability" can be made by the metric

misconception: When a skill appears suddenly as models grow, something new must have switched on inside the bigger model.
objective: The learner can explain that with 10-token answers scored all-or-nothing, models improving steadily from 50% to 95% per token score 0.1% to 59.9%, near zero and then a jump, so an apparent sudden ability can come from the metric rather than the model.

claims.text: In the toy, a 10-token answer is fully right with probability p^10 when each token is right with probability p independently (stage caption under the chart: 'Toy: each token right or wrong independently'; reveal: 'ten tokens all right is p to the tenth power, which stays tiny until p is near 1').
claims.source: Product rule for independent events; independence is the toy's stated assumption. exact() in Demo.tsx.

claims.text: For p = 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 and 95%, p^10 is 0.098%, 0.60%, 2.8%, 10.7%, 34.9% and 59.9% (stage and reveal round to one decimal: 0.1%, 0.6%, 2.8%, 10.7%, 34.9%, 59.9%); scored per token the same models read 50% to 95%; with 1-token answers the whole-answer score equals p.
claims.source: Arithmetic (node, 2026-10-14, cm-ai brief); WHOLE and ONE in Demo.tsx MODEL block. Values in the reveal are recorded when the learner presses each preset.

claims.text: Some reported 'emergent abilities' of large language models look sudden under all-or-nothing metrics such as exact match and smooth under continuous or per-token metrics (reveal: 'Before calling an ability emergent, check whether a smoother score shows it growing all along').
claims.source: Schaeffer, Miranda and Koyejo (2023), 'Are emergent abilities of large language models a mirage?', NeurIPS 2023 (arXiv 2304.15004); original emergence reports: Wei et al. (2022), 'Emergent abilities of large language models', TMLR. About real systems; the lesson advises a check and does not claim every case is an artifact.

recall.question: A benchmark counts an answer only if all 20 of its steps are right. Across model sizes the score jumps from 2% to 40%. What should you check before calling it a new ability?
options: Whether a per-step score rose smoothly across the same sizes
Whether the biggest model has more layers
Nothing; a jump that large must be a new ability
recall.why: All-or-nothing scoring raises per-step accuracy to a high power, which sits near zero and then shoots up. A per-step score can show steady growth hiding under the jump.
